correctness.rationale: Definition 6 specifies lexicographic primary covered voters and secondary PAV-like second-stage score. Strong nonnesting on 3 candidates forces unique winning singleton A and unique winning pair BC. Singleton strict approval scores give u+q>v+r and u+p>w+r, while pair coverage implies u<=v,w; any equality contradicts secondary comparison, hence v,w>=u+1. Therefore q,p>=r+2 and n>=6+3u+3r+t+e. Equality forces u=r=t=e=0, v=w=1, p=q=2; BC covers all 6 while AB and AC cover 5, and A singleton has support4 versus3. Independent exhaustive enumeration checked all 3002 anonymous ballot-count vectors with 1..6 voters (including empty ballots): exactly 3 nonnested at 6. Finite census does not replace the all-n inequality.

value.rationale: A sharp smallest electorate for forced nonnesting is an interpretable boundary of a recently proposed approval-rule house-size criterion. The strict inequalities and uniqueness classification explain why tie-breaking cannot rescue the witness.

final_claim: For irresolute Adams-AV on exactly three candidates with arbitrary unweighted approval ballots and committee sizes 1 and 2, strong tie-independent failure of nesting needs at least six voters; exactly three labeled anonymous six-voter profiles, relabelings of AB,AB,AC,AC,B,C.
limitations: Precisely three labeled candidates, committee sizes 1 and 2, unweighted anonymous ballot multisets; no 4+-candidate minimality.
